name: paper_trading_v2
description: Build Paper Trading V2 system per spec. Reuse v1 modules (paper_trading/*.py). Replace Streamlit with Python GUI (PySide6 or Dear PyGui). Multi-symbol config registry, per-symbol Signal Engine, Risk Guard with block bootstrap kill-switch, Execution Layer with auto-MCP-reconnect, token input via GUI. 4-tab GUI: Symbol Onboarding, Live Control, Performance Monitor, Account & Connection.

members.name: Architect_Lead
members.executionPrompt: You are the Lead Architect. Your job: 1) Decide GUI framework (PySide6 vs Dear PyGui) per spec section 7.1, explain the choice. 2) Design the directory structure: configs/symbols/*.yaml, paper_trading_v2/ with adapted v1 modules. 3) Write the _template.yaml for new symbols. 4) Write the v2_frozen.yaml as the single source of truth. 5) Integrate all modules into run.py entry point. 6) Ensure auto-MCP-reconnect logic is in every module that calls MCP. The MCP token should be configurable via GUI input (not just env var). Output: directory tree, config files, run.py, integration wiring. Reuse v1 code from paper_trading/ wherever possible.

members.name: GUI_Dev
members.executionPrompt: You build the Python GUI following the framework chosen by Architect_Lead. The spec (section 7.2) requires 4 tabs: Tab1 Symbol Onboarding (7-step wizard with hard gates), Tab2 Live Control (dropdown per symbol, automation level switch per symbol, pending signals table, open positions, emergency stop button always visible), Tab3 Performance Monitor (per-symbol metrics table, equity curve chart, kill-switch status with manual override), Tab4 Account & Connection (MT5 account info display — RED fullscreen if not demo, MCP status, reconnect button, MCP token input field). Design: ALL controls are immediate-response (no web reload). Emergency Stop button is RED, always visible, fixed position. Every destructive action needs a second confirmation dialog. Automation level resets to 1 on every startup. Log every user action to the logger DB. The GUI must NOT use Streamlit. Output: main GUI Python file + any helper files.

members.name: Signal_Engine_Dev
members.executionPrompt: You adapt the v1 signal_engine.py for V2 multi-symbol architecture. Key changes: 1) Read config from configs/symbols/{SYMBOL}.yaml per symbol (not a single v2_frozen.yaml). 2) Validate status field — only 'validated' symbols get a running engine. 3) Per-symbol model artifacts from artifacts/models/{SYMBOL}/. 4) Per-symbol feature_schema from artifacts/feature_schemas/{SYMBOL}/. 5) Maintain separate levels_cache per symbol. 6) Entry = next open after confirmation. Stop = sweep_extreme + buffer_atr. Target = entry + reward_r * (entry - stop). 7) No-lookahead: all rolling windows use shift(1). Reuse the v1 sweep_detector_v2, confirmation, feature_pipeline, rule_score modules from paper_trading/src/. Output: updated signal_engine_v2.py module + any necessary adapters.

members.name: Risk_Execution_Dev
members.executionPrompt: You adapt v1 risk_guard.py and execution_layer.py for V2. For Risk Guard: 1) Dynamic asset registry (not hardcoded XAUUSD/EURUSD) — read from configs/symbols/*.yaml. 2) Per-symbol kill-switch with block bootstrap (CI lower bound < 1.0 after min_trades per config). 3) Per-symbol position sizing from config. 4) For new validated symbols (from onboarding), start with size_multiplier ≤0.5 and lower min_trades (e.g. 15). For Execution Layer: 1) Auto-reconnect on EVERY MCP call (not just at init) — wrap every _call_mcp with retry+reconnect. 2) MCP token can be set dynamically (not just from env var) — add set_token() method. 3) Magic number 20791 on every order. 4) Comment format: 'LSW-V2-{event_id}'. 5) Log BEFORE sending order (section 5 of spec). 6) Handle MCP disconnect during an open position — polling positions every 30s. 7) Graceful degradation: if MCP down, keep GUI alive showing disconnected state. Output: updated risk_guard_v2.py and execution_layer_v2.py.

members.name: Logger_SharedState_Dev
members.executionPrompt: You adapt v1 logger.py and shared_app_state.py for V2. For Logger: 1) Schema matches spec section 5 exactly (add 'asset' column, features_json, kill_switch_status_at_signal, automation_level). 2) Add user_action_log table: timestamp, action_type, details_json — for tracking GUI user actions (change automation level, override kill-switch, send order button click). 3) Ensure log_signal() is called BEFORE order is sent (entry_planned/stop/target recorded first). 4) Add function to query recent trades per symbol for Risk Guard. For Shared State: 1) Dynamic asset registry (not hardcoded). 2) Thread-safe with RLock. 3) Snapshot includes ALL fields the GUI needs. 4) Add mcp_connection_state field (connected/disconnected/reconnecting). 5) Add mcp_token field (settable via GUI). 6) Emergency stop flag that stops ALL signal engines immediately. Output: updated logger_v2.py and shared_app_state_v2.py.

tasks.subject: Knowledge Base — Error Patterns & Fixes for all team members
tasks.description: Create paper_trading_v2/KNOWLEDGE_BASE.md with sections: 1) MCP Connection errors: 'MCP_TOKEN not set' → check env var or GUI input. '401 auth failed' → wrong token. 'Connection refused' → MT5/MCP bridge not running. 'port not found' → wrong port. 2) MCP Tool errors: 'tool not found' → wrong tool name, check list_tools(). 'Invalid params' → check schema. 3) MT5 errors: 'symbol not in MarketWatch' → add_symbol() first. 'Invalid volume' → check min/max lot. 'No connection' → MT5 terminal disconnected. 4) Signal Engine errors: model.pkl not found → check path. Feature mismatch → check feature_schema. 5) Risk Guard errors: insufficient trades for bootstrap → show message. 6) Auto-reconnect: always wrap MCP calls with retry+reconnect. 7) GUI: PySide6 event loop blocking → use QThread for background polling.

findings.problem: configs/symbols/XAUUSD.yaml and EURUSD.yaml are missing the `status` field (required by spec section 1: 'status: validated | candidate | rejected'). The whole safety mechanism — Signal Engine only runs for validated symbols — depends on this field.
findings.requiredFix: Add `status: validated` to XAUUSD.yaml and EURUSD.yaml, and `status: candidate` with comment explaining never auto-validated to _template.yaml.

findings.problem: Dashboard (dashboard.py) uses Streamlit (import streamlit as st) — spec section 7 explicitly says 'Không dùng Streamlit/web-based cho phần điều khiển chính'. The spec requires a Python GUI (PySide6 or Dear PyGui) with 4 tabs. No GUI with 4 tabs exists.
findings.requiredFix: Replace Streamlit dashboard with a proper desktop GUI (PySide6 or Dear PyGui) with 4 tabs per spec section 7.2: Symbol Onboarding, Live Control, Performance Monitor, Account & Connection.

findings.problem: No run.py entry point exists. run_trading.py is the entry point but spec section 8 requires a run.py following the specified startup order. No dedicated run.py file found anywhere.
findings.requiredFix: Create run.py as the entry point per spec section 8 startup order.

findings.problem: execution_layer.send_order() does NOT set magic_number=20791 on MCP orders. Spec section 2.3 requires a fixed magic_number (e.g. 20791) on every order. The method doesn't pass any magic_number parameter to the MCP call at all.
findings.requiredFix: Add magic_number=20791 to order_params in execution_layer.send_order() per spec section 2.3.

findings.problem: execution_layer.send_order() uses default comment='paper_trade_v2'. Spec section 2.3 requires comment format 'LSW-V2-{event_id}' to include the event identifier for distinguishing system orders from manual ones.
findings.requiredFix: Change default comment to f'LSW-V2-{event_id}' (or similar) using the actual event_id per spec section 2.3.

findings.problem: execution_layer does not implement set_token() method. The spec mentions MCP token should be input-able via GUI. The current code reads token only from env var (MCP_TOKEN) at construction time with no runtime setter.
findings.requiredFix: Add set_token(token: str) method to ExecutionLayer class so the GUI can update the MCP token at runtime.

findings.problem: No KNOWLEDGE_BASE.md exists anywhere in the workspace. All team members need documentation of error patterns and fixes.
findings.requiredFix: Create KNOWLEDGE_BASE.md with error patterns, fixes, and operational guidance for all team members.

findings.problem: Signal engine (signal_engine.py) reads from a single v2_frozen.yaml config (line 83) rather than per-symbol config from configs/symbols/{SYMBOL}.yaml as required by spec section 4. The engine does not validate the `status` field.
findings.requiredFix: Modify create_check_new_bar() to load per-symbol config from configs/symbols/{SYMBOL}.yaml and validate status=='validated' before starting.

findings.problem: Signal engine loads model from a single model path (_MODEL_DIR / 'model.pkl'), not per-symbol model artifacts from artifacts/models/{SYMBOL}/ as required by spec section 4.
findings.requiredFix: Load per-symbol model from artifacts/models/{SYMBOL}/model.pkl and calibrator.pkl per spec section 4.

findings.problem: execution_layer._parse_mcp_response() at line 59 returns a tuple (result, _extract_result_text) instead of a plain dict when content list is empty — but _extract_result_text reference is undefined. This is a syntax/runtime error.
findings.requiredFix: Fix line 59 to return result (plain dict) instead of the invalid tuple.

findings.problem: RiskGuard._refresh_asset line 249: base_asset normalization logic uses asset.rstrip('m') for symbols like XAUUSDm/EURUSDm but then checks against 'XAUUSD'/'EURUSD' hardcoded strings.
